question: Which of the following uses spores to reproduce?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Ferns**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ferns** reproduce via spores, which are typically found on the underside of their fronds.
 
• Spores are a common reproductive method for non-flowering plants such as ferns, mosses, and fungi.
 
• Unlike seeds, spores are usually single-celled and do not contain stored food resources.
 
• Spores can be dispersed by wind, water, or animals, allowing the plant to spread to new locations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Yeast** reproduces primarily through budding, a form of asexual reproduction.
 
• **Amoeba** reproduces by binary fission, another form of asexual reproduction.
 
• **Mango** trees reproduce through seeds and vegetative propagation, not spores.
 
• Spores are a key feature of the life cycle of many plants and fungi, enabling them to survive in various environments and conditions.
